newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Aug 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Aug 5.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The need to seek assistance through a bailout programme from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) shows the country is facing its greatest crisis, former prime minister Anand Panyarachun says. Anand, who is chairman of the Constitution Scrutiny Committee, says the move demonstrates that Thailand is confronted by a serious, deep-rooted crisis of faith and political bankruptcy. (BANGKOK POST)

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh faces a no-confidence debate late next month, the crunch period for politics when Parliament is also expected to vote on the constitution draft. As the opposition whips agree on the delicate censure timetable, Chavalit's troubles mount with New Aspiration Party MPs asserting that his pledge to support the charter draft does not represent the party's stand. (THE NATION)

- Education Minister Sukhavich Rangsitpol says he will lead the talks with Acer Group, a sponsor of the Bangkok Asian Games next year, to resolve some legal points in the sponsorship contract. He expects the talks to resume soon between the Taiwan-based computer giant and the Bangkok Asian Games Organising Committee and hopes the company will have no objection to accepting conditions which will help resolve the legal points. (BANGKOK POST)

- Nomination of the new permanent secretary for finance will be on the agenda of the Cabinet today as an urgent issue and Comptroller-General Nibhat Bhukkanasut is tipped to be the prime nominee. Nibhat has become the prime contender because of his previous record of dealing with international issues such as coordinating with the International Monetary Fund. (BUSINESS DAY, THE NATION)

- The government has agreed to allow independent power producer (IPP) licensees to renegotiate the terms governing tariffs of power sales to the Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand. The government's move is aimed at assisting the seven winning IPP bidders to weather the impact of the depreciation of the baht. (BANGKOK POST)
